verdicts.strongest_argument: The finding concedes its own refutation in its second sentence: 'The quote is three months old and was priced once, in the -13.78% June reaction.' A CFO statement made on a public earnings call on 2026-06-03, describing the assumption set inside guidance the company issued, is the 90-100 anchor almost verbatim - it restates published guidance. And the corpus proves the transmission: docs/e5819b95...txt carries the exact Sullivan quote at 2026-06-04T10:14:51Z, immediately beneath a headline in the same feed reading 'Why Is FIVE Stock Cratering Over 10% In Overnight Trading?' at 2026-06-04T09:30:05Z. So the market not only saw the assumption, it attributed the entire 13.78% single-day loss to it. The move from there to 'not priced' is the one inference this role exists to block: the hunter argues the fact was 'unpriced again by a 75.5% rally off the low', which is using the run-up as a substitute for an option chain it does not have. A rally does not un-publish a disclosure. Worse for the claim, the three upgrades it cites - Mizuho 2026-07-09, Bernstein 2026-07-21, Jefferies 2026-08-13 - all post-date the June call, so the analysts doing the re-rating were underwriting a guide whose tariff-reversion assumption was already on the record; the hunter's own independence note says Mizuho published H2 comps of 8-9% and $9.22 EPS 'above consensus', which is a sell-side house explicitly modelling the back half the assumption covers. Nor is the claim's residue material: 'the H2 guide rests on a policy assumption that may not hold' is generically true of every tariff-exposed retailer's guidance in 2026 and carries no sized number - the hunter itself calls the magnitude 'small' and the band 'genuinely two-sided'. The one thing I grant is real: this print is the first forum where the assumption is either reaffirmed or cut, and no captured item revisits it after 2026-06-04. That is a timing observation, not new information, and it is worth the ten points I withhold, not more.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Publishes the CFO's back-half tariff-reversion assumption verbatim on the morning after the call, in an article whose framing is that the shares slid despite a profit beat.
Same feed carries 'Why Is FIVE Stock Cratering Over 10% In Overnight Trading?' - the market's attribution of the drop to this disclosure, published the same day.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Wolfe Research cut FIVE to hold in June - the bear case on the back half was already being published by sell-side within three weeks of the call.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The fact was priced in one measured event: the 2026-06-03 amc print produced -13.78%, the largest reaction in the seven-event history and 2.5x the 5.59% median. That is the market pricing this exact disclosure. Since then run_up_20d is +8.44% and the stock sits 7.48% off its 52-week high at 243.08, but I decline to use the rally as a pricing argument in either direction - it is not an implied-move substitute. Note the 5-day run-in is -5.54%, so even the recent tape is not the one-way melt-up the 'unpriced again' argument needs.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated pre-print source showing sell-side H2 models had quietly removed the tariff-reversion assumption (or a specific tariff-rate datapoint between June and September that made reversion measurably impossible), so that the guide and consensus had drifted apart by a quantified amount.

interactions: The claim and its Mizuho corroboration cut against each other: the hunter uses Mizuho's above-consensus H2 forecast as evidence the bull case 'requires H2 to beat', but a published sell-side H2 model dated after the June call is evidence the assumption was re-underwritten, which is the opposite of 'nobody re-underwrote it'.
corpus_limits: The FIVE capture has no news items - it is an EDGAR index plus a Stocktwits dump - so I cannot see full preview or analyst-note bodies, only the upgrade/downgrade headlines relayed in the social feed; I cannot therefore verify whether any of those notes discussed the tariff assumption, and I have not treated the absence as evidence either way. No options chain, so no implied move. The eight Form 4s of 2026-08-04/05 have no stored bodies, so their direction is unknowable in this corpus.
